items.headline: Microsoft Build opening keynote ships Foundry, Work IQ, and the MAI model family
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday Build was still ahead of the event: coverage was a session-catalog preview plus a weekend leak naming three narrow MAI debuts (MAI-Image 2.5, MAI-Voice 2, MAI-Transcribe 1.5) and pointing at the Windows Agent Framework MIT release. Today the keynote actually opened at Fort Mason and the shipments are concrete and broader than the leak suggested. The MAI story is no longer three media models but a full in-house family anchored by a coding model positioned to power GitHub Copilot, framed explicitly as reducing OpenAI dependence. New named artifacts that did not appear yesterday: Azure AI Foundry as the orchestration layer (3,000+ model marketplace) with Claude running as a first-class alternative to GPT through Claude Code, the Work IQ Microsoft 365 grounding layer, and Agent 365 as the enterprise control plane, alongside Office Copilot Agent Mode and a more autonomous GitHub Copilot. The prediction-shaped leak from yesterday has resolved into the actual launch.

items.headline: Snowflake Platform Keynote wires Claude into Cortex AI with Snowflake Intelligence and Cortex Code
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's coverage was the Sunday-evening opening keynote framing — Ramaswamy on stage with Anthropic's Daniela Amodei — and a forward pointer to the Tuesday Platform Keynote, with no specific product announcement yet. Today the Platform Keynote (Dageville and Kleinerman, 9:00 AM PT) actually delivered the substance: Snowflake will integrate Anthropic's Claude directly into Cortex AI, extending the ~$200M December partnership and letting 13,900+ customers run Claude agents against governed data without it leaving the platform. The agentic control plane now has two named pieces absent yesterday — Snowflake Intelligence (knowledge-worker agent) and Cortex Code / 'Coco' (coding agent) — plus named early adopters (Carvana, eSentire, Notion) and the Openflow / Adaptive Compute / Cortex AISQL roadmap. The Amodei appearance shifted from a billed keynote pairing to a quoted argument that trust accelerates business.

items.headline: BadHost Starlette host-header flaw puts the open-source LLM serving stack in scope
items.diff_narrative: No precedent in yesterday's news. This is a fresh security thread: BadHost (CVE-2026-48710), a host-header injection flaw in Starlette (the routing core under FastAPI, ~325M downloads/week) that defeats path-based authentication middleware with a single character. The affected surface reaches directly into the local-LLM serving stack — FastAPI, vLLM, LiteLLM, and MCP servers (whose unauthenticated OAuth discovery endpoints give a reliable exploitation path) — with chains to auth bypass, SSRF, and in some cases RCE. It was found by X41 D-Sec during an OSTIF-sponsored vLLM audit; the fix shipped in Starlette 1.0.1 on May 21, and the disclosing researchers argue the assigned 6.5 CVSS understates the downstream impact.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot flips every plan to usage-based billing
items.diff_narrative: Not present yesterday. GitHub Copilot switched all plans to usage-based billing on June 1, retiring flat-rate premium requests in favor of GitHub AI Credits metered against per-model token rates, and removing the prior cheaper-model fallback once an allowance is exhausted. The change drew sustained developer pushback with projected 10x-50x cost jumps (one $29 to $750, another $50 to $3,000). The item ties directly into today's Build delta: the metered billing and the cheaper first-party MAI coding model are framed as two halves of the same margin story, a connection that did not exist in yesterday's corpus.

items.headline: Bay Area June-July events rollup
items.diff_narrative: The recurring events rollup carries forward with the calendar advanced one day, and the state-change is that the two lead events are now mid-keynote rather than pending. Yesterday Snowflake Summit was 'opens tonight at 5:00 PM PT' and Build was 'runs tomorrow'; today both are happening live — Snowflake's Platform Keynote in progress with the Builder Keynote still ahead Wednesday, and Build's Nadella keynote already streamed. Still-upcoming items (WWDC June 8-12, Databricks June 15-18, AI Engineer World's Fair June 28-July 2, plus GitHub Universe and AWS re:Invent further out) are carried forward; the AI Tinkerers VIP Dinner is now 'tonight.' Yesterday's Voice Agents Science Fair detail is not surfaced today, while the Advanced MCP Showcase remains.
